content.title: What is a Palindrome?
content.description: A palindrome is a sequence that reads exactly the same forward and backward.

content.content: Palindrome problems are among the most popular topics in coding interviews. They test your understanding of strings, arrays, two-pointer techniques, and optimization strategies.

content.title: Fun Fact
content.content: The word 'MADAM', number '1221', and phrase 'NITIN' are all examples of palindromes.

content.title: Palindrome Example
steps: Forward: M A D A M
Backward: M A D A M

content.content: Understanding Palindromes
A palindrome remains unchanged when reversed. Palindromes can be strings, numbers, arrays, or even sentences after removing spaces and special characters.

content.title: Key Observation
content.description: A palindrome is symmetric around its center. Characters at equal distances from the center must match.

content.content: Checking Whether a String is a Palindrome
The simplest palindrome problem is determining whether a given string reads the same forward and backward.
Two Pointer Technique
The most efficient palindrome validation method uses two pointers. One starts from the beginning and the other from the end. Both move toward the center while comparing characters.

content.title: Interview Favorite
content.content: The Two Pointer approach is the most commonly expected solution during coding interviews.
Palindrome Numbers
Palindrome concepts are not limited to strings. Numbers can also be palindromes if their digits remain the same after reversal.
Longest Palindromic Substring
This famous interview problem asks us to find the longest contiguous substring that is a palindrome.

content.title: Center Expansion Idea
content.description: Every palindrome has a center. Expand outward while characters match to find the maximum palindrome length.

content.content: Palindrome Permutation
Some problems ask whether characters of a string can be rearranged to form a palindrome.

content.title: Important Rule
content.content: For a palindrome permutation, at most one character can have an odd frequency.
Applications of Palindromes

items.question: DNA Analysis
items.answer: Biologists search for palindromic patterns in DNA sequences.

items.question: Text Processing
items.answer: Used in pattern recognition and linguistic analysis.

items.question: Cryptography
items.answer: Palindrome patterns help in sequence analysis.

items.question: Competitive Programming
items.answer: Frequently appears in coding contests and interviews.

content.content: Palindrome vs Non-Palindrome
Real-Life Analogy

content.title: Mirror Reflection
content.content: Imagine looking at a perfectly symmetrical object in a mirror. Both halves appear identical. A palindrome behaves similarly because it looks the same from both directions.

content.title: Interesting Fact
content.content: Some natural DNA sequences contain palindromic regions that play important roles in biological processes.
Common Mistakes

items.question: What is the most common mistake?
Why do comparisons fail?
items.answer: Spaces and special characters are not removed.

items.question: Why is Two Pointer preferred?
items.answer: It validates palindromes efficiently using constant space.

content.title: Interview Insight
content.description: Whenever a problem mentions symmetry, reverse matching, longest palindrome, or palindrome permutations, consider Two Pointers, Hash Maps, or Center Expansion.

points: A palindrome reads the same forward and backward.

Center Expansion is a popular optimization technique.
Palindrome permutation depends on character frequencies.
